rated_messages.input_message: Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.
Sometimes an urge comes on like a wave. Imagine what it is like to ride the wave as it ebbs and flows. Instead of trying to swim against it, try riding it out until it disappears into the sea.
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
If you get urges, remind yourself that cigarettes did that to you. If you go back to them, they will keep making you suffer. Now you are breaking free.

Add the phrase “I’m having the thought that…” in front of your unhelpful thoughts. For example, “I’m having the thought that I need a cigarette.” Your thoughts are not always true or helpful! They are just thoughts.

To keep on track, small changes can really help. For example, keep a list of quit reasons where you used to keep cigarettes, rearrange your living space, or grab some extra pens to fiddle with to keep your hands busy.
Maybe you could use these few minutes to work out whose birthday is next and what message you'll write in their card? Then when it comes you'll have something original and well thought-out to write!
When you begin to crave a cig, concentrate on your reasons for not smoking. Keep a list on your phone and look at it when you feel yourself beginning to falter.
Take a slow, deep breath in. And let it out. Now, ask yourself, "Am I willing to go one minute without smoking?" When that minute is over, ask yourself this question again.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
